acceptance: The supported ParadeDB image and extension combination is pinned and documented, and the adapter fails clearly when pg_analytics is missing
_supported_tuning_type_names matches what the adapter actually applies
Applied layout requests are verified against the catalog; skipped ones are recorded with a reason
Live TPC-H SF0.01 tuned run, with the evidence recorded in the PR
context: Done. PR #3206 squash-merged. Adapter requires pg_search (pg_analytics is gone from current ParadeDB images) and names pinned image paradedb/paradedb:0.26.2-pg18; heap PARTITIONING/CLUSTERING/SORTING applied and verified against the catalog (pg_get_partkeydef, pg_index.indisclustered per partition) with honest ledger on partial failure. Also fixed a latent shared-base defect: PostgreSQLAdapter ran CLUSTER inside a transaction (reproduced on plain postgresql: 2 executed / 4 failed); the hardened flow now lives in PostgreSQLAdapter and pg_duckdb keeps only its routing guard. Live TPC-H SF0.01 seed 42 PASSED on paradedb and postgresql (22 queries, validation PASSED, 6 executed/0 failed/0 dropped). Fast suite 30484 passed. Changelog entry added. Container removed.
description: ParadeDB declares PARTITIONING and CLUSTERING as supported (benchbox/platforms/paradedb.py:123) but skips both at execution (paradedb.py:33-34: execution_partitioning_supported = False, post_load_index_cluster_supported = False). The claimed support doesn't match what happens. Work out the right layout method for ParadeDB's storage: pg_analytics/DuckDB-backed tables and heap tables. Either implement it with ledger evidence, or stop claiming the tuning types. The current ParadeDB image (paradedb/paradedb:latest, checked during the #3092 work) no longer ships pg_analytics, which the adapter requires ("extension \"pg_analytics\" is not available"), so first settle which ParadeDB image and extension combination is supported.
